headline: Light is the fastest thing in the universe—nothing can outrun it
universal_truth: What we see is always the past; even the present moment takes time to reach our eyes
fun_facts: Light travels at 186,000 miles per second—it could circle Earth 7.5 times in one second
The light from the Sun takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach your eyes
When you look at a star, you're seeing light that left possibly thousands of years ago
discussion_questions: How does knowing we always see the past change your perception of 'now'?
What 'light' do you want to bring into the world?
Where in your life do things seem dark that might just need a new angle?

hook.script: Right now, light is racing toward your eyes at 186,000 miles per second. By the time you process this sentence, light could have circled Earth seven times. Today, we chase the fastest thing in the universe.

cliff.script: Nothing can travel faster than light—it's the universe's speed limit. But here's what's strange: light can act like a wave AND a particle at the same time. How is that possible?

options.response: Yes, but that's only half the story...

options.text: Both waves and particles—it depends how you measure
options.response: Exactly. Light's nature changes based on how we observe it. Mind-bending, right?

fact1.title: The Universal Speed Limit
fact1.script: Light travels at 299,792,458 meters per second—and nothing with mass can ever reach that speed. As you approach light speed, time itself slows down. At exactly light speed, time would stop. Einstein showed us this in 1905.

fact2.title: Seeing the Past
fact2.script: The sun you see right now is actually the sun from 8 minutes ago. Look at the night sky—that star might not even exist anymore. Some starlight has traveled for millions of years to reach your eyes. We're all time travelers.

fact3.title: Wave-Particle Mystery
fact3.script: Light behaves as a wave until you try to observe individual photons—then it acts like particles. This quantum weirdness kept Einstein puzzled his whole life. The act of observation changes what we observe.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: We are literally made of light. Every atom in your body was forged in a star, created through nuclear fusion—a process that releases light. You're stardust, still glowing.

outro.script: That's Day 4. Tomorrow, we'll explore how sound moves through the world. Until then, notice the light around you—it's been traveling since before you were born.

growTrack.title: Illumination - Finding Light
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify sources of positivity and insight in your life
growTrack.activity: Make a list of three things that 'light you up'—activities, people, or places that energize you. Circle one you could spend more time with this week.
